# Deere & Company (NYSE: DE): strategy analysis with a focus on Construction & Forestry

Note: I researched this on 3 October 2026. Deere's fiscal year ends around 1 November. "Fiscal 2025" means the year ended 2 November 2025. The latest quarter is the third quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended 2 August 2026. Revenue shares are my own arithmetic from the reported figures.

## Company snapshot

- Deere makes agricultural, turf, construction, forestry and roadbuilding equipment and also finances it. It has manufactured agricultural equipment since 1837 and was incorporated in Delaware in 1958. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
- Headquarters: One John Deere Place, Moline, Illinois.
- Public company, listed on the NYSE as DE, and files with the SEC. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release, SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
- Revenue, fiscal 2025: worldwide net sales and revenues were $45.684 billion, down 12% from $51.716 billion. Equipment net sales were $38.917 billion. ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release, SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
- Profit, fiscal 2025: net income was $5.027 billion ($18.50 per diluted share), down 29% from $7.100 billion in fiscal 2024. ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
- Employees: about 73,100 at 2 November 2025, of whom about 32,500 were full-time production employees. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
- Latest quarter (Q3 fiscal 2026, ended 2 August 2026): net income was $1.379 billion ($5.10 per share), up 7%. Net sales and revenues were $12.608 billion, up 5%. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
- Fiscal 2026 guidance: net income of $4.75–5.00 billion, raised in August. Management says 2026 will mark the bottom of the current ag equipment cycle. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))

## Business units

- **Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA)**
  - What it sells: large tractors, combines, cotton and sugarcane harvesters, tillage, seeding and spraying equipment, and precision technology.
  - Who buys: production-scale growers of grains, cotton and sugarcane. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
  - Fiscal 2025: net sales of $21.406 billion, about 38% of worldwide net sales and revenues, and operating profit of $2.671 billion. ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
- **Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT)**
  - What it sells: utility and compact tractors, hay and forage equipment, mowers, golf and turf equipment, and utility vehicles.
  - Who buys: dairy and livestock producers, high-value and small-acre crop growers, and turf and utility customers. Some turf products are sold through The Home Depot and Lowe's. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
  - Fiscal 2025: net sales of $10.224 billion, about 22% of the total, and operating profit of $1.207 billion. ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
- **Construction & Forestry (C&F)**
  - What it sells: excavators, motor graders, dozers, loaders, backhoes, articulated dump trucks, compact equipment, forestry machines, and Wirtgen Group roadbuilding equipment (Wirtgen, Vögele, Hamm, Kleemann, Benninghoven, Ciber). ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
  - Who buys: residential, commercial and public construction contractors, infrastructure and roadbuilding contractors, rental companies, and forestry operators. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
  - Fiscal 2025: net sales of $11.382 billion, about 25% of the total, and operating profit of $1.028 billion. ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
  - Its share is growing. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026, C&F sold $10.079 billion, about 28% of net sales and revenues. In Q3 its $3.618 billion of sales came close to PPA's $3.998 billion. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
- **Financial Services (John Deere Financial)**
  - What it does: finances retail purchases of new and used Deere equipment from dealers, offers leases, and sells extended warranties. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
  - Fiscal 2025: revenue of $5.821 billion, about 13% of the total, and net income of $1.114 billion. ([Deere Q4/FY2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
- Note: the four segments add up to about 98% of the total. The rest is other revenue that I did not break down.

## Industries and main competitors

Deere's 10-K names the main rivals. In construction they include Caterpillar, CNH, Doosan Bobcat, Hitachi, Komatsu, Kubota, Volvo CE, SANY and XCMG. In agriculture they include AGCO, CLAAS, CNH, Kubota and Toro. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))

**1. Construction and compact construction equipment (C&F)**

- **Caterpillar**
  - Strength: bigger scale and higher margins. Its Construction Industries segment sold $8.346 billion in Q2 2026 at a 23.3% segment profit margin. Deere C&F's margin was 12.1% in its comparable quarter. ([Caterpillar Q2 2026 earnings release, SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm); [Deere Q3 FY2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
  - Weakness: a larger tariff burden. It expected about $2.6 billion of incremental tariff costs in 2026. Deere expects a net tariff headwind of about $750 million. ([Investing.com, Caterpillar Q4 2025 slides](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/caterpillar-q4-2025-slides-record-revenues-despite-margin-pressure-from-tariffs-93CH-4473727); [Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))
- **Komatsu**
  - Strength: a global construction and mining franchise worth ¥4,132.8 billion in sales, with a 13.7% operating margin for the year to March 2026. ([Komatsu FY results, March 2026](https://www.komatsu.jp/en/newsroom/2026/20260428_1))
  - Weakness: it expects both sales and profit to fall this fiscal year because of U.S. tariff costs and lower mining demand. Deere, by contrast, raised its guidance. ([Komatsu FY results](https://www.komatsu.jp/en/newsroom/2026/20260428_1))
- **Volvo Construction Equipment**
  - Strength: ahead on electrification. It is delivering L120 Electric wheel loaders, and its adjusted operating margin for 2025 was 13.3%. ([Volvo CE Q4 2025 results](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tractor))
  - Weakness: shrinking sales. 2025 net sales fell to SEK 81.6 billion from SEK 88.3 billion. Deere C&F sales are guided up about 20% for fiscal 2026. ([Volvo CE Q4 2025 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-ce-demonstrates-better-earnings-in-q4-2025/); [Deere Q3 FY2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
- **Kubota**
  - Strength: a strong position in compact equipment. It described its North American construction machinery market as steady in 2025, supported by housing and public construction. ([Kubota FY2025 financial results](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/136q4e.pdf))
  - Weakness: its construction equipment sales fell in 2025, and its operating profit fell 15.9%, mainly because of U.S. tariff costs. ([Kubota FY2025 financial results](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/136q4e.pdf))

**2. Agricultural equipment (PPA and SAT)**

- **CNH Industrial (Case IH, New Holland)**
  - Strength: a milder 2026 decline in ag sales. It guides ag net sales down 5% to flat. Deere guides PPA down about 10%. ([CNH FY2025 results](https://investors.cnh.com/news/news-details/2026/CNH-Industrial-N-V--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx); [Deere Q3 FY2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
  - Weakness: much lower profitability. Its 2025 ag adjusted EBIT margin was 6.2%, while Deere PPA earned $2.671 billion on $17.311 billion of sales. ([CNH FY2025 results](https://investors.cnh.com/news/news-details/2026/CNH-Industrial-N-V--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx); [Deere FY2025 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465925116130/de-20251126xex99d1.htm))
- **AGCO (Fendt, Massey Ferguson, PTx)**
  - Strength: Fendt is gaining share, including in North American large ag. Its PTx retrofit precision business added 14 products in 2025. ([AGCO FY2025 results](https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-02-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-2025-FULL-YEAR-RESULTS))
  - Weakness: smaller and less profitable, with 2025 sales of $10.1 billion and a 7.7% adjusted operating margin. ([AGCO FY2025 results](https://news.agcocorp.com/2026-02-05-AGCO-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-2025-FULL-YEAR-RESULTS))
- **Kubota (small ag and turf)**
  - Strength: global reach. 77.3% of its revenue is from outside Japan, and it forecasts revenue growth to ¥3,150 billion in 2026. ([Kubota FY2025 financial results](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/136q4e.pdf))
  - Weakness: its North American tractor sales were held back by dealer inventory reduction in 2025. ([Kubota FY2025 financial results](https://www.kubota.com/ir/financial/release/data/136q4e.pdf))

**3. Roadbuilding, forestry and equipment finance**

- Note: the 10-K names Fayat and GOMACO in roadbuilding and Ponsse and Tigercat in forestry. I did not find current figures for them, so I give no strengths or weaknesses. Banks and leasing companies compete with John Deere Financial, but I did not research them.

## Environmental scan

Note: this PESTLE scan covers the Construction & Forestry (C&F) segment only.

**Political**
- Tariff relief helps. Section 232 tariffs on certain agricultural and construction equipment were cut from 25% to 15% from 8 June 2026 to 31 December 2027. That lowers costs on imported machines and components. ([AEM, Section 232 tariff changes](https://www.aem.org/news/section-232-tariff-changes-what-manufacturers-need-to-know))
- Federal road funding is uncertain, which hurts. The authorities under the 2021 infrastructure law (IIJA) expired on 30 September 2026. A stopgap continuing resolution extends highway programs only to 11 December, at prorated FY2026 levels. That clouds roadbuilding (Wirtgen) demand beyond 2026. ([NACo](https://www.naco.org/news/iija-authorities-expire-september-30-naco-urges-congress-uphold-full-funding-levels-highway); [AASHTO Journal](https://aashtojournal.transportation.org/house-passes-senate-cr-to-extend-federal-gov't-funding/))

**Economic**
- Data-center and energy building is a strong tailwind. Data-center construction starts reached $84.1 billion through July 2026, nearly three times the year before. Deere cites data-center, infrastructure and energy projects as the reason C&F order books run "well into fiscal year 27". ([ConstructConnect, Sept 2026 data center report](https://news.constructconnect.com/september-2026-data-center-report-year-to-date-spending-nearly-three-times-a-year-ago); [Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))
- Rising interest rates are a headwind. On 16 March 2026 the Fed raised its target range to 3.75–4.00% because inflation remains elevated. That makes equipment finance and housing more expensive. ([Federal Reserve FOMC statement, 16 Sept 2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetary20260916a1.pdf))

**Social**
- Construction labor is scarce, which cuts both ways. 87% of contractors have hourly craft openings, and 42% say shortages have delayed projects. Delays can slow equipment purchases, but scarcity also pushes customers toward productivity tools such as grade control. ([AGC, 2026 workforce survey](https://www.agc.org/news/2026/09/03/construction-workforce-shortages-remain-acute-despite-soft-market-conditions-data-centers-strain))
- Housing activity is flat, which hurts compact equipment and forestry. U.S. housing starts were 1.275 million (annualized) in August 2026, 1.2% below August 2025. Deere expects global forestry to be down about 10% because residential construction is subdued and log and lumber prices are softer. ([U.S. Census Bureau, New Residential Construction, Aug 2026](https://www.census.gov/construction/nrc/pdf/newresconst.pdf); [Deere Q3 FY2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))

**Technological**
- Precision construction technology helps. Factory-installed SmartGrade adoption is up more than 50% year to date, and job-site safety solution sales are up nearly 40%. ([Motley Fool, Deere Q3 2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))
- Deere now owns its excavator design. After the Hitachi joint venture ended in 2022, Deere took over the factories and full control of its excavator design. It launched three Deere-designed excavator models, with more due through 2030. This gives it product control, but it must now fund that development itself. ([Construction Equipment, Deere–Hitachi JV ends](https://www.constructionequipment.com/earthmoving/news/10758870/john-deere-hitachi-end-jv); [Deere Q3 FY2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))

**Legal**
- Right to repair is a risk. In July 2026 Deere settled the FTC's case and agreed, for 10 years, to give farmers and independent shops the same repair tools as its dealers. The settlement covers farm equipment only. ([FTC press release, July 2026](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/07/ftc-states-secure-settlement-deere-company-advancing-farmers-right-repair))
  - Note: my own inference is that construction customers could push for the same terms, which would threaten C&F parts and service margins. This is not sourced.
- Engine-emissions laws add cost. The U.S., EU, India and others keep tightening off-road engine emissions rules. Compliance needs significant investment in engines and after-treatment, which raises product costs. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))

**Environmental**
- Customers want lower emissions, which is an opportunity with a timing risk. Deere says it plans to offer hybrid-electric and battery-electric construction equipment to help customers cut tailpipe emissions. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf))
  - Volvo CE is already delivering electric wheel loaders, so being late would hurt Deere in emissions-sensitive markets. ([Volvo CE Q4 2025 results](https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/news-and-events/news-and-stories/2026/volvo-ce-demonstrates-better-earnings-in-q4-2025/))
- Weaker timber markets hurt forestry. Global forestry demand is expected down about 10% in fiscal 2026. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 outlook exhibit, SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d2.htm))

## Research summary

- **C&F has become Deere's growth engine while farm demand bottoms out.** C&F sales rose 18% and operating profit rose 84% in Q3 fiscal 2026, while PPA sales fell 6%. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
- **The demand mix is shifting from housing to large projects.** Data centers, infrastructure and energy are driving earthmoving orders, while residential-linked forestry is falling. That supports large equipment and Wirtgen more than compact equipment and forestry. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [ConstructConnect](https://news.constructconnect.com/september-2026-data-center-report-year-to-date-spending-nearly-three-times-a-year-ago))
- **Margins are improving but still trail Caterpillar.** C&F is guided to a 10.5–11.5% operating margin for fiscal 2026, against Caterpillar's 23.3% Construction Industries margin in Q2 2026. That gap is the strategic question for C&F. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [Caterpillar Q2 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000040/ex991toformcat2q2026earnin.htm))
- **Policy is the biggest swing factor.** Deere expects net tariffs of about $750 million in fiscal 2026 and about $1 billion in fiscal 2027. Federal highway funding is on a stopgap only to 11 December 2026. ([Deere Q3 FY2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); [AASHTO Journal](https://aashtojournal.transportation.org/house-passes-senate-cr-to-extend-federal-gov't-funding/))
- **Technology is Deere's main way to differentiate in construction.** It is applying its precision-ag technology (cameras, obstacle detection, the Operations Center) to construction, and SmartGrade adoption is accelerating. ([Deere 2025 Form 10-K](https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_downloads/2025/12/Deere-Company-2025-10-K.pdf); [Deere Q3 FY2026 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/21/deere-de-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))

- **Deere plans to spin off Construction & Forestry.** Management said on the Q3 call that C&F will be listed as a separate company in 2027. ([Deere Q3 fiscal 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))

## Limits of this analysis

- Note: Deere is a public company, so its figures come from SEC filings and are not estimates.
- Note: the segment revenue shares are my own arithmetic from the reported totals. The four segments add up to about 98% of the total, and I did not trace the remainder.
- Note: I could not find Deere's market share in construction equipment, or a profit split between Wirtgen and the rest of C&F, in the sources I read.
- Note: I did not find data on roadbuilding and forestry competitors (Fayat, GOMACO, Ponsse, Tigercat) or on finance competitors, so they get no strength or weakness assessment.
- Note: I used a Motley Fool transcript for the earnings-call detail (tariff amounts, SmartGrade adoption, rental share, backlog), not a Deere-issued transcript.
- Note: Caterpillar's 2026 tariff estimate comes from an Investing.com summary of its slides, not the filing itself.
- Note: competitors report on different fiscal calendars and in different currencies (yen, kronor), so the cross-company comparisons are approximate.

## Summary

Deere & Company (Moline, Illinois; fiscal 2025 revenue $45.7 billion, net income $5.0 billion, about 73,100 employees) is relying on its Construction & Forestry segment while large-ag demand bottoms out. In Q3 fiscal 2026, C&F sales rose 18% and operating profit rose 84%, helped by data-center, infrastructure and energy projects. The key risks for C&F are tariffs, uncertain IIJA highway funding, a Fed rate hike to 3.75–4.00%, weak housing and forestry, and a persistent margin gap with Caterpillar.
